concepts.title: Cell Theory and Classical Discoveries
concepts.definition: The foundational biological principles asserting that all living organisms are built of cells and cell products, with new cells arising exclusively from pre-existing cell division.
concepts.formula: All living units = pre-existing cells + cellular products
concepts.key_idea: Cells form the universal both structural and functional basis of life, generated solely through pre-existing cellular division.
question_patterns: what are the main tenets of modern cell theory
who proposed that new cells arise from pre-existing cells
explain the contribution of Schleiden, Schwann, and Virchow to cell theory
describe how cell theory was formulated and modified
state the core principles of cellular organisation in living organisms

solution_steps.explain: Recognize Leeuwenhoek's first description of living cells and Brown's subsequent discovery of the nucleus.
Botanical and zoological findings established that plants and animals consist of cells and cell products.
Integrate 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' to specify that all new cells originate from divisions of existing cells.

concepts.title: Prokaryotic Cell Envelope and Modifications
concepts.definition: A complex three-tiered protective covering in prokaryotes comprising an outer glycocalyx, middle cell wall, and inner plasma membrane, along with specialized membrane infoldings like mesosomes.
concepts.formula: Cell envelope = glycocalyx + cell wall + plasma membrane
concepts.key_idea: Prokaryotic cell envelopes provide protection, structural stability, and specialized infoldings for replication and respiration.
question_patterns: what is a mesosome in a prokaryotic cell and what are its functions
describe the three layers of the bacterial cell envelope
how do Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria differ in cell envelope response to staining
explain the role of flagella, pili, and fimbriae in bacterial cells
identify bacterial surface structures involved in motility and attachment

solution_steps.explain: Identify outer glycocalyx (loose sheath or tough capsule), cell wall, and selectively permeable plasma membrane.
Recognize mesosomal extensions as sites for cell wall synthesis, DNA replication, secretion, and respiration.
Differentiate motile flagella from non-motile surface attachment structures like pili and fimbriae.

concepts.title: Prokaryotic Ribosomes and Inclusion Bodies
concepts.definition: Membraneless 70S ribonucleoprotein particles involved in protein translation, alongside non-membrane bound cytoplasmic granules that store reserve nutrients.
concepts.key_idea: Prokaryotes utilize membrane-associated 70S ribosomes for translation and naked cytoplasmic inclusions for nutrient storage.
question_patterns: what are polysomes or polyribosomes in bacterial cells
describe the subunits and function of prokaryotic ribosomes
what are inclusion bodies and give examples found in bacteria
how do gas vacuoles assist photosynthetic bacteria
how does prokaryotic ribosomes and inclusion bodies work

solution_steps.explain: Note that 70S ribosomes consist of 50S and 30S subunits associated with the plasma membrane.
Describe how multiple ribosomes attach to a single mRNA strand to translate proteins concurrently.
List non-membrane bound reserve stores such as phosphate, cyanophycean, and glycogen granules.

concepts.title: Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport
concepts.definition: A fluid mosaic phospholipid bilayer with mosaic both integral and peripheral proteins that mediates cell growth, secretion, passive diffusion, osmosis, and active ion pumping.
concepts.key_idea: The lipid bilayer's fluid nature allows protein movement and selectively regulates molecule exchange across cell boundaries.

explain the fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson
how do neutral solutes and polar molecules move across the plasma membrane

Subtract total defined percentage from 100 to find carbohydrates and other constituents.
Confirm the other_percentage is non-negative and represents carbohydrates and other non-protein non-lipid constituents of the membrane.

concepts.title: Cell Wall and Intercellular Junctions
concepts.definition: A non-living rigid outer layer in plants, fungi, and algae that provides structural integrity, protection against infection, and intercellular connection via plasmodesmata.
concepts.formula: Middle lamella = calcium pectate adhesive layer
concepts.key_idea: Plant cell walls provide mechanical strength while middle both lamellae and plasmodesmata join neighboring cells.
question_patterns: what is the chemical composition of algal and plant cell walls
explain the role of calcium pectate in the middle lamella
what are plasmodesmata and what function do they serve
describe the difference between primary and secondary cell walls
list the main features of cell wall and intercellular junctions

solution_steps.explain: Recognize cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins in plant cell walls and galactans/mannans in algae.
Identify calcium pectate as the middle layer that glues adjacent cell walls together.
Detail how cytoplasmic channels traverse cell walls to link neighboring plant cell cytoplasms.

concepts.title: Endomembrane System and Vacuolar Dynamics
concepts.definition: A functionally coordinated organelle network comprising the ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles that works together to synthesize, modify, package, and segregate cellular products.
concepts.key_idea: Coordinated membrane organelles process and route proteins, lipids, and cellular wastes inside eukaryotic cells.

concepts.title: Mitochondrial Structure and Energy Generation
concepts.definition: A double-membrane organelle containing folded inner cristae, circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, and respiratory enzymes responsible for generating ATP through aerobic respiration.
concepts.formula: Mitochondrial lumen = outer compartment + inner matrix
concepts.key_idea: Mitochondria act as cellular powerhouses, producing ATP across inner membranes expanded by cristae infoldings.
question_patterns: describe the structural organisation of a mitochondrion
why are mitochondria termed the power houses of the cell
what is the function of cristae in mitochondria
mention the semi-autonomous features present in mitochondrial matrix
how does mitochondrial structure and energy generation work

solution_steps.explain: Identify the outer continuous limiting membrane and inner membrane folded into cristae.
Recognize circular DNA, RNA, 70S ribosomes, and proteins necessary for semi-autonomous function.
Explain how cristae increase surface area for ATP synthesis during aerobic metabolism.

concepts.title: Plastids and Chloroplast Architecture
concepts.definition: Pigment- or nutrient-storing double-membrane organelles in plants, including light-harvesting chloroplasts organized into fluid stroma and stacked thylakoid grana.
concepts.key_idea: Chloroplasts harvest solar energy within thylakoid membrane stacks to synthesize organic compounds in the stroma.

solution_steps.explain: Distinguish photosynthetic chloroplasts, pigmented chromoplasts, and storage leucoplasts.
Differentiate starch-storing amyloplasts, oil-storing elaioplasts, and protein-storing aleuroplasts.
Identify double membrane boundary, stroma matrix, light-trapping thylakoids stacked as grana, and stroma lamellae.

concepts.title: Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture
concepts.definition: Motility and structural organelles made up of tubulin protein arrangements, featuring a 9+2 axoneme array in cilia/flagella and a cartwheel triplet pattern in centrioles.
concepts.key_idea: Nine radially arranged peripheral microtubule doublets surrounding two central singlets form the core eukaryotic locomotory axoneme.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the 9 peripheral doublets by 2 to get individual peripheral microtubules.
Add the 2 central singlet microtubules to the peripheral count.
Confirm the total matches the canonical 9+2 arrangement, yielding 20 individual microtubules for a standard eukaryotic axoneme.

concepts.title: Nuclear Structure and Chromosome Morphologies
concepts.definition: A double-membrane bound nuclear envelope containing nucleoplasm, nucleoli, and chromatin, which condenses into distinct chromosomes categorized by centromere location.
concepts.key_idea: Nuclear DNA packages into chromatin and distinct chromosomes classified into metacentric, sub-metacentric, acrocentric, or telocentric using centromere position.

solution_steps.explain: Divide total meters of DNA by total number of chromosomes in the genome.

Mesosomes assist in cell wall formation, DNA replication, daughter cell distribution, respiration, secretion, and increasing membrane surface area.
